title: Batching Strategist: workload signature profiling and guarded continuous-apply engine
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Build a 'Batching Strategist' service that continuously profiles live workload signatures, synthesizes conservative batching/caching parameter recommendations, and applies them via a guarded continuous-apply pipeline with automatic rollback on quality or SLO regressions. This ticket covers the profiling heuristics, recommendation scoring, safety checks, and the apply/rollback orchestration (not the UI).

Background: We have many experiments that show per-workload token distributions and KV cache hit patterns vary across tenants and time-of-day. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone. Previous batch recommenders either over-aggressively increase batch sizes (causing tail latency spikes) or are too conservative to affect cost. The Strategist should strike a balance: measurable cost savings (10–25% per workload) while keeping P95 latency and error-rate within configured SLOs.

Success metrics (analytics):
- mean cost-per-1k-tokens for pilot workloads reduced by >= 12% within 2 weeks of rollout
- no more than 2% regression in P95 latency for targeted workloads
- automated rollback triggers fire and complete within 90s when regressions detected
- recommendation precision (precision@top3) >= 0.78 measured against labeled good/bad outcomes

Acceptance criteria: 
- service computes workload signatures (sequence length histogram, KV reuse ratio, burstiness metric, model variant compatibility) and stores lightweight fingerprints in time-series store
- recommendation engine produces ranked parameter sets (max_batch_tokens, max_concurrent_requests, kv_cache_ttl, prefix_cache_enabled) with a safety score and confidence band
- guarded apply pipeline that stages changes to a shadow routing tier, collects telemetry for a shadow window, evaluates SLO and quality checks, and promotes or rolls back automatically according to policy
- rollout policy supports canary-by-tenant, gradual ramp (% traffic), and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants
- detailed runbook and smoke tests for rollback scenarios and emergency aborts

Technical approach: 
1) Profiling: agent-side lightweight fingerprint collector (C++) integrated in runtime router; reports per-route histograms and KV cache indicators every 2m into metrics pipeline (Prometheus + Timescale). Privacy: samples are aggregated and no raw prompts are retained.
2) Heuristics: hybrid model combining rule-based signals (e.g., high kv_reuse && short median_length -> safe for larger micro-batches) with a small gradient-boost model trained on historical apply outcomes. New features: burst_coalescence_index and kv-temporal-stability.
3) Recommendation scoring: multi-objective score weighing cost delta vs latency risk vs quality risk. Output a confidence interval and safety_score in 0..1.
4) Continuous-apply orchestration: orchestrator creates a 'shadow-profile' deployment which mirrors traffic for measurement (sidecar sampling or shadow copies depending on tenant). Shadow window config default 5 minutes with 90s minimum. Evaluate metrics from runtime-1.23 dashboards and the model-quality webhooks (evaluations service).
5) Rollback criteria: triggers include P95 latency increase > configured threshold, error-rate spike, or quality regression measured by prompt test-suite. When triggered, orchestrator performs immediate rollback and files a rationale event to the audit log and Slack incident channel.
6) Telemetry & audit: every apply must be accompanied by a deterministic diff, experiment id, and link to the recommendation rationale stored in Confluence.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Shadow window length: shorter windows reduce time-to-save but increase false-positive noise. Default 5m chosen; we allow tenant overrides.
- Conservative defaults for kv_cache_ttl vs aggressive quantization: prioritize latency stability for enterprise tenants.
- ML-driven recommendations vs deterministic rules: use hybrid approach to improve explainability for SRE/Support.

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Should we allow recommendations that change model variant (e.g., from fp16 to a quantized variant) as part of the same apply? Current proposal: allowed only if model compatibility flag is set and security_review for the variant has passed.
- Standardize safety_score threshold per customer tier (free vs paid vs enterprise)?

Runbook & rollback plan: 
- Preflight: smoke test of recommendation on canary 1% for 1h with synthetic traffic if workload is low.
- Shadow apply: collect 5m of traffic; evaluate; if pass, ramp to 10% then 25% over configurable intervals.
- On trigger: orchestrator snapshots previous config, routes traffic back, posts incident to #infra-ops with exp id, and correlates with the session traces for RCA.

Next milestones (this ticket):
- prototype profiler pipeline + fingerprint schema validated (week 1–2)
- rule-set prototype and scoring function implemented (week 3)
- shadow-apply orchestrator scaffolding + telemetry hooks (week 4)

Notes: This ticket intentionally excludes Console UI work; PM will open separate tickets for rollout controls. Integration with Dedicated capacity autoscaler will be covered in a follow-up after initial pilot.
